legs.bout: Alexander Hernandez vs Rafael Dos Anjos

bets.reasoning: Hernandez at -300 (FD 71.5% no-vig, ours 80.8%). Dos Anjos is 42, two years out after knee surgeries, and cutting to 155 where his cardio has failed before. Model and read agree. Staked about half quarter-Kelly since the favourite price caps the payoff.

Parkin at +110 (FD 45.4%, ours 52.9%). Walker's chin has failed against heavy hitters and heavyweight punches are heavier. Model already leans Parkin and Sherdog's Feely picks him by KO. Risk is Parkin's 18-month layoff, so stake is slightly under quarter-Kelly.

weeks.note: First card, so small and selective. All 28 fighters made weight; the only late change was McGhee's three-day-notice opponent, where the model's 46% for Romero against FanDuel's 20% is the model being uninformed, so no bet. Most of the sheet's top EV is method/round props (decision, goes the distance), which are model-derived and only half-shrunk toward the price. I distrust them on this card: Soldic, Wint and Smith are finishers against short-notice or power-punching opponents, and Sherdog's picks lean to early finishes. Skipped those. I took two moneylines where the model and our reads agree and there is a stylistic reason: Hernandez over a 42-year-old dos Anjos two years off after three knee surgeries, and Parkin over Walker, whose chin has failed against heavy hitters. Stakes are well under quarter-Kelly because the edges are a few points and the market is sharp.

weeks.event: UFC Fight Night: Allen vs. Duncan
weeks.note: A card where the sheet's loudest numbers are the model's general lean toward decisions and moneyline gaps my reads don't back (Kamaka, Tanzilovi), so most of it is a pass. I bet only two decision props with a fight-specific reason, small, because both rest on the finish model rather than a proven moneyline edge. Weigh-ins: Souza, Ribeiro and Bonfim (7.5 lb) missed; none touches these bets. Allen and Duncan both made weight.

legs.bout: Brendan Allen vs Christian Leroy Duncan

bets.reasoning: Five rounds between a grinder who wins late and a striker who has never been submitted: Allen's path is control and a decision, and Duncan's knockouts come early against lesser opposition, not against a durable top-five middleweight. FanDuel's 40% for the distance looks low for this matchup; I make it about half.

legs.bout: Allen Frye Jr. vs Rj Harris

bets.reasoning: Harris is the deserved favourite (about 73%), but Frye has never been finished (his only UFC fight went the distance) and comes in 15 lb lighter at 246, so a Harris win on the cards is likelier than FanDuel's 14.5%. Small stake: heavyweight finish rates make this a long shot either way.

bets.reasoning: Croden by KO/TKO at +340 (about 23% implied). Four of her last six wins are by strikes, mostly late ground-and-pound as opponents fade, and she has never been finished. Chandler was stopped by strikes in round 1 by Edwards, has missed weight twice at 135 and says she is fighting through injuries. With Croden a -330 favourite, even a 45% KO share of her wins puts this near 34%. Small stake: method props rest on thinner modelling.

Daukaus at -200 (63% no-vig) against our 70%: the line drifted from -235 toward Barriault with no news behind it, the kind of home-country money a Canadian card draws. Barriault is 36, 1-5 in his last six and calls this the last chapter; he presses forward, which feeds Daukaus's front-headlock chokes, and the pundits go 11-3 Daukaus. Daukaus's chin against power (Nickal) is the risk, so about a quarter-Kelly stake.

weeks.note: Two pick'em title fights and a lot of chalk. The moneylines are sharp: the model's biggest gap (Evloev, 57% vs an even line) runs against our own read on Volkanovski, so no side there. The edges with a reason are in the distance markets of the two title fights (two five-round fights between fighters who rarely finish each other or get finished) and Pico by decision after his fight-week change of approach. Small stakes: these are prop edges of a few points, sized below quarter-Kelly. Passed on the Yakhyaev-Krylov round props (they bet against Yakhyaev's round-one record) and on Volkov by decision (no reason beyond the number).

bets.reasoning: Volkanovski-Evloev to go to decision at -225 (65% implied, 71% ours). Evloev has never finished a UFC opponent and said this month he will try to win over five rounds rather than chase a finish; Volkanovski's two knockout losses came against elite power punchers, which Evloev is not, and Volkanovski's own finishes against wrestlers are rare.

Yan-Dvalishvili to go to decision at -320 (71% implied, 78% ours). Neither man has ever been finished, their two fights went 15 and 25 minutes, and Dvalishvili's volume wrestling and Yan's patient boxing both suit a long fight.

Pico by decision at +310 (21% implied, 30% ours). Pico's path is wrestling Keita, who has never faced an elite wrestler and took the fight on a short turnaround, and this week Pico said he will build fights instead of rushing them, which is how he beat Pitbull 30-27. If Pico wins, it is most likely on the scorecards.

legs.bout: Farman Hasanov vs Jean Paul Lebosnoyani

bets.reasoning: Lebosnoyani by decision at +320 (24% implied, 27% ours). The market makes him a 76% favourite but prices a decision at only 21%, i.e. it expects him to finish about three of every four wins. Both of his UFC wins went the full 15 minutes, and Hasanov has never been stopped: a chain wrestler who kept shooting while tired and took Eric Nolan the distance. If Lebosnoyani wins, the scorecards are the likeliest way.

Kropschot by KO/TKO at +360 (22% implied, 28% ours). Klein was stopped by strikes in round two of both his UFC fights, each time after spending himself in a big first round, and Kropschot survives early danger and finishes in R1-R2. The market prices Kropschot's wins as mostly submissions from his record, but Klein's own losses say a fading Klein gets stopped by strikes.

weeks.event: UFC Fight Night: Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker
weeks.note:
Wednesday early check of the Nov 7 card. One prop with a reason: FanDuel prices Elijah Smith's finish as a knockout first (KO +210, about 32% no-vig; submission +470, about 17.5%), but Davey Grant has never been knocked out in 26 pro fights while being submitted five times, most recently in R1 by Charles Jourdain in October 2025. Smith's last win was a rear-naked choke after a knockdown. The decision and round props on the main event and Petroski-Kondratavicius show positive EV on the sheet, but the finish rates of a Walker five-rounder and a fast-starting puncher against a chin-first wrestler explain the market's numbers; passing those. Small stake: method props rest on the finish model, shrunk halfway to the market.

Friday read on the Nov 7 card, after weigh-ins (no misses reported) and 162 pundit picks. Wednesday's Elijah Smith by submission stands. One addition: Cortes-Acosta on the moneyline. Walker has been stopped six times, gets knocked out when opponents press, and moves into a heavyweight division where Cortes-Acosta (262) has never been stopped; heavyweight underdogs have lost money over the line in all three eras since 2016. The five-round format, the one spot where dogs have beaten the line, keeps the stake moderate. Passing on the long list of decision and 'starts round N' props: they rest on the finish model, and the main-event ones bet on Walker surviving 15+ minutes, which his record argues against. Petersen and Bashi lean my way in the reads but the prices (-170, -550) leave no edge.

bets.reasoning: Grant's stoppage losses are all submissions (5) and none by KO in 26 fights; the market leans Smith's finish toward KO. If Smith stops a 40-year-old who gives up his neck in scrambles, the submission is the likelier way. Ours 23.8% vs FanDuel 15.4% at +470.
Walker's chin against heavyweight power (six KO/TKO losses, four in R1) and a heavyweight underdog at 32%; ours 74.8% vs FanDuel 68.0%.

weeks.note:
Thursday early check. Nov 7: the props showing EV (Walker main event to decision or to round 4/5, Souza or Delano by decision) rest on the finish model, and the reads give no reason the market's finish rates are wrong; the Wednesday Smith-by-submission bet stands as placed. UFC 334: one moneyline. Stephen Thompson is 43, 16 months out after his shin was split to the bone, on a three-fight skid, and lost the grappling in all three losses; Charles Radtke's last two wins came from takedowns, back takes and long control. The market still makes the retiring legend a slight favourite. The edge is modest (51% vs 47%) and partly in the model already, so the stake is small. Radtke was knocked out by strikers twice (Prates, Malott), which is why this isn't bigger.

The two title fights are priced about right. The model, the market and the pundits all side with Gane and Harrison, so there's no edge on either winner. The edges I trust are small: (1) Duncan, where the model is far above the line (84% stats-only against 61%) and the matchup backs it: his front-headlock chokes against a 38-year-old who has been stopped three times since 2023, with eight of nine pundits on Duncan. (2) Gane by decision: Hokit has never been stopped and Gane wins by range, not violence, over five rounds. (3) A little more on Radtke at a better price than Thursday's +102. I'm passing on the McKinney-fight round props: the sheet's timing is league-average and ignores that 17 of McKinney's 18 finishes came in R1. Hasan at -1250 is too short, and there's no line yet on Diaz. Total $4 on an $81.71 bankroll, sized well under quarter-Kelly because these edges are thin.
